job.title: Senior Development Engineer
job.description:
A metropolitan Melbourne council is looking for an experienced Senior Development Engineer to join its Drainage & Development team. The role suits an engineer with a strong local government background in development and subdivision engineering.

About the role: Reporting to the Coordinator Drainage & Development, within Infrastructure & Environment (Asset Management), you will assess the engineering aspects of developments and recommend planning, building and development conditions. You will also implement the Special Building Overlay, so that new developments are protected from flooding and new infrastructure meets Council standards.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Assessing engineering aspects of planning permit and subdivision applications
• Reviewing and approving engineering plans and computations
• Inspecting subdivision works and issuing Statements of Compliance
• Assessing stormwater drainage and WSUD, and undertaking flood modelling assessment
• Formulating engineering conditions for private development and subdivision approvals
• Providing technical support to developers, including legal points of discharge
• Providing customer advice on the Special Building Overlay
• Coordinating Town Planning and Building application assessments with other council departments
• Reviewing developers' Construction Management Plans as requested

About you: You bring proven experience in a similar role within local government or a comparable organisation, and you are comfortable liaising with developers, consultants and authorities.

• A degree in Civil Engineering (Bachelor of Civil Engineering), with National Engineering Register (NER) status with Engineers Australia
• Demonstrated development or subdivision engineering experience, with knowledge of the Subdivision Act 1988 and IDM
• Proficiency in civil design, drainage assessment and construction management
• A good understanding of building regulations, planning regulations, land surveying and flood modelling

Experience with SPEAR, AutoCAD, 12d Model and Pathway is relevant to the role. Experience with a growth area council is also of interest.

What's on offer:

• Band 6A – 6C under the council's enterprise agreement
• A senior position within a specialist drainage and development team
• Varied work spanning assessment, inspection, negotiation and technical advice
• The opportunity to mentor junior engineers

About the role: Reporting to the Team Leader Development Management, you will assess, issue, coordinate and regulate permits for works and occupation within Council's road reserves. The aim is to ensure works are undertaken safely, with minimal impact on the community and Council assets.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Acting as the primary contact for applicants, contractors and developers on permit requirements and compliance
• Managing enquiries and resolving issues, liaising with internal departments to avoid conflicts in the public realm
• Preparing reports, correspondence and recommendations on permit applications, inspections and compliance
• Maintaining records in permit databases, document management and CRM systems
• Supporting permit data collection and analysis, contributing to procedure and system improvements, and mentoring less experienced officers

About you: You bring proven experience assessing, determining and issuing road reserve works, road occupation and filming permits, along with a firm understanding of traffic management principles, reinstatement standards and asset protection requirements.

TC1/TMI1 and TC2/TMI2 (non-practitioner) certificates are essential for this role. You will also have:

• A current Traffic Management Designer category 1 roads (TMD 1) certificate of attainment
• A current valid Victorian Driver's Licence
• The ability to interpret temporary traffic management plans, civil drawings and reinstatement specifications

Experience in a regulatory or compliance environment in local government or a similar sector, and a TMD2 (non-practitioner) certificate, would be well regarded.

• Band 5A – 5D under the council's enterprise agreement

The Company

Their business has grown, but the roastery is still at the heart of what they do. They are now looking for a skilled Coffee Roaster to join the production team and help deliver consistent, high-quality coffee to customers across the country.

The Role
Reporting to the roastery leadership, the Coffee Roaster will run roasting operations day to day. You'll make sure every batch meets the business's standards for quality, consistency and flavour.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Operating commercial roasting equipment to agreed roast profiles and production schedules
  • Monitoring roasts and adjusting variables to keep each batch consistent
  • Taking part in cupping and quality control to evaluate roasted coffee and green beans
  • Helping develop and refine roast profiles for new and existing blends and single origins
  • Managing green bean stock, including receiving, storage, rotation and inventory records
  • Keeping accurate production and batch records for traceability
  • Carrying out routine cleaning and basic maintenance of roasting equipment
  • Following food safety, quality and workplace health and safety requirements at all times
  • Supporting packing and dispatch as needed to meet production deadlines

This is a great opportunity for someone who is passionate about coffee and enjoys hands-on production work in a stable Monday to Friday role. The hours are 8am to 5pm.

Requirements
The ideal candidate will bring:

  • Proven experience as a coffee roaster in a commercial roasting environment
  • Strong knowledge of roasting principles, roast profiling and the factors that affect flavour development
  • Cupping and sensory evaluation skills
  • An understanding of green coffee, including origins, processing methods and quality grading
  • Experience with roasting software and data logging. This is highly regarded
  • Knowledge of food safety and quality standards in a production setting
  • Strong attention to detail, and a commitment to consistency

job.title: Bid Coordinator
job.description:
About the Role

If you’ve recently qualified as a carpenter and want to move off the tools, this role turns your site knowledge into a career in estimating.

A privately-owned commercial and industrial builder in Ballarat needs a Bid Coordinator in its pre-construction team. You’ll work on live tenders from day one, with coaching, and take on more packages and whole tenders as you develop.

Key Responsibilities

  • Use your site knowledge to review plans and specifications and develop trade scopes
  • Phone subcontractors and suppliers for pricing and build complete scopes
  • Compare quotes by trade and prepare comparison sheets
  • Prepare bills of quantities and tender pricing in costing software
  • Work with the pre-construction, design and project teams


Essential Requirements

  • Carpentry or related trade qualification, ideally recently completed, with site experience
  • Able to read plans and specifications and break work into trade scopes
  • Confident on the phone chasing and negotiating pricing
  • Strong Excel and Microsoft Office skills
  • Based in or near Ballarat, working in the Ballarat office 5 days a week


Desirable Extras

  • Certificate IV or Diploma of Building and Construction, completed or in progress
  • Estimating or construction software experience (helpful, not essential)


What’s on Offer

  • $80,000 + super, with the package set for someone moving off the tools into estimating
  • Permanent, full-time, with an established privately-owned builder
  • Coaching and a clear path to running your own tenders


How to Apply

Simply click the Apply button, answer the screening questions and attach or up-to-date resume. Aspect Personnel is recruiting for a confidential client and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds.

job.title: Junior Maintenance Administrator
job.description:
About the role

Our client, a disability housing provider based in Melbourne CBD are seeking a Junior Maintenance Administrator to join their team. Working closely with the Facilities manager, you will take ownership of incoming maintenance requests from their large portfolio of homes across Victoria and South Australia. The successful candidate will have excellent problem solving skills and use their judgement to resolve what they can, and allocate the rest to the designated person.

Key responsibilities

  • Review incoming maintenance requests and decide whether each can be resolved through quick troubleshooting, or needs to go to the facilities team, a contractor or a tenancy manager
  • Work with residents and support staff to resolve minor issues without a call-out
  • Track all open requests, follow them up and make sure nothing is missed
  • Reconcile completed work against contractor invoices before payment
  • Monitor maintenance spend against budget and flag anything trending over
  • Liaise with the facilities, tenancy and accounts teams


About you

  • 1–2 years’ experience in a property management or facilities administration role
  • Good judgement and confidence on the phone, including troubleshooting.
  • Well organised, with strong attention to detail.
  • Confident with Excel and experience using CRM systems (Zoho experience is a bonus, but not essential)
  • Experience in SDA, NDIS or the disability sector is desirable but not essential


Essential requirements

  • Ability to obtain an NDIS Worker Screening Clearance and a National Police Check

job.title: Finance/AP Officer
job.description:
About the company and team:

An established commercial construction business based in Melbourne's east, delivering projects across a diverse range of sectors. You'll join a small, close-knit finance team that reports to the CFO - a trusting, flexible and caring manager. You'll be trained and supported by an experienced colleague who knows the full AP and payroll function. Construction industry or Jobpac experience is a bonus but not essential, as full training is provided. More importantly, they're looking for someone who will be a great fit for the team: a strong communicator and team player who is proactive, enjoys solving problems, and genuinely cares about their role, the business and the people around them.

What's on offer

  • Flexible working arrangements considered.
  • 4 wellbeing days a year (one each quarter, after probation)
  • EOFY and Christmas functions, plus regular team lunches
  • Annual review every November, with a performance bonus
  • A stable, focused AP role, with the chance to build skills in payroll and broader finance over time
  • A January start, so you can enjoy Christmas before beginning

Key Responsibilities

  • Full-cycle accounts payable: invoice processing, supplier reconciliations, employee expenses, and weekly and month-end payment runs
  • Month-end reconciliations and journals (general ledger and credit cards)
  • Support with BAS, PAYG and other compliance reporting
  • Back-up payroll support, including entitlements, super, Incolink and Co-invest (training provided)
  • Support financial controls and audits, and liaise with internal and external stakeholders

Key Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years' experience in a similar role and a demonstrated stable work history
  • Construction industry experience preferred, but other industries will be considered
  • Experience with accounting systems (familiarity with Jobpac is a bonus)
  • Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
  • Strong team player with a positive can-do attitude
  • Pro-active approach and a natural problem solver
  • Strong communication skills both written and verbal
